To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a combination of enzymes (xylanase, cellulase, and pectinase) increased apparent total tract digestibility of energy in corn and DDGS fed to pigs.

the inclusion of enzymes in diets for growing pigs can increase the digestibility of energy from corn and corn DDGS and the concentration of energy in the pig, and this increase in energy digestibility and concentration can be further increased by feeding a diet containing 10% DDGS and 1.0% of an enzyme mixture.
the addition of exogenous enzymes to the corn DDGS diets of pigs improved the apparent total tract digestibility of energy, nitrogen, and amino acids.

the development of a new technology that will allow for the efficient utilization of corn co-products in swine diets.
the evaluation of exogenous enzymes for improving the digestibility of nutrients in high fiber corn co-product diets for pigs.
the development of a new generation of enzymes for improving the nutritional quality of corn co-products.
